goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
goldens.reasoning: Both point out that a backup code component is named TwoFactor.

goldens.comment: Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login
goldens.reasoning: Both say the message mentions 'backup code login' even though this is the disable endpoint.

goldens.comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
goldens.reasoning: Both describe backup code validation failing on uppercase input because the case is not normalized.

goldens.comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
goldens.reasoning: Both describe a race condition where two concurrent requests can reuse the same one-time backup code.

goldens.comment: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
goldens.reasoning: Both flag the backup code object URL never being revoked, which leaks memory. One says it happens on unmount and the other on reset or modal close, but it is the same leak.

candidates: Default-exported component is named TwoFactor but the file/component is for backup codes, making stack traces/React DevTools misleading
Log message says 'backup code login' but endpoint is disabling 2FA, making operational logs misleading when diagnosing failures
Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex but user input isn't normalized - uppercase input from password managers would be rejected even if the code is correct
Backup code consumption is not atomic: two concurrent login attempts with the same backup code can both pass indexOf() before either update runs, allowing one-time code reuse
resetState() doesn't clear/revoke the generated ObjectURL for the backup-codes download, causing Blob URL leaks when modal is closed/reopened multiple times
Password visibility toggle button is removed from tab order via tabIndex={-1}, making it inaccessible to keyboard-only users
UI always shows success toast after navigator.clipboard.writeText even though it can reject (permissions, insecure context), giving false 'copied' success for backup codes
backupCodes are decrypted and JSON.parse'd without validation/handling in the login flow - if encryption key changes or data is corrupted, this throws an unhandled exception

backupCodes are decrypted and JSON.parse'd without validation/handling in the disable endpoint - if encryption key changes or stored value is corrupted, JSON.parse will throw and crash the endpoint instead of returning structured error
